results.target: shows an overview of our rule-guided LLM solution for OUD CP using structured EHR data and clinical narratives from UF Health. Physician chart-reviewed labels are used as the gold standard.
results.answer: Overview of the OPRO framework. Clinical narratives and evidence rubrics are used to generate extraction prompts, which are then processed by GPT-oss-120b to produce item-level judgments.

results.question: axes
results.target: The proposed LLM-based CP is composed of three components: an LLM engine (gpt-oss-120b15) that extracts evidence and determines the met/not-met binary judgments with supporting text evidence, and then a logistic regression model that uses the LLM- extracted indicators to generate patient-level OUD probabilities.
results.answer: The OPRO pipeline.

results.question: trend
results.target: We compared our LLM-based CP with a diagnosis code–based phenotype, a machine learning-based CP using structured EHR features, NLP-derived features, and their combination, and a zero- shot LLM without rule guidance.
results.answer: The OPRO framework extracts evidence items from clinical narratives, converts them into item-level judgments, and uses logistic regression to predict a patient-level OUD probability, which is then converted into a performance score.
